### R

```{r}
#| label: convex-hessian-3d-r
#| echo: !expr knitr::is_html_output()
#| eval: !expr knitr::is_html_output()
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   Surface plot of f(x) = exp(2 x1 + x2) - x1 for x1 from -1 to 1 and x2
#|   from -3 to 3. The surface is a trough that rises steeply toward the
#|   upper right, where 2 x1 plus x2 is large, and is nearly flat on the
#|   lower left. A dashed vermilion straight line along the direction (1, -2)
#|   through the origin lies on the surface, because f is linear there.
ch_x1_sf <- seq(-1, 1, length.out = 101)
ch_x2_sf <- seq(-3, 3, length.out = 101)
ch_grid_sf <- tidyr::expand_grid(x1 = ch_x1_sf, x2 = ch_x2_sf)
ch_u_sf <- 2 * ch_grid_sf$x1 + ch_grid_sf$x2
ch_value_sf <- exp(ch_u_sf) - ch_grid_sf$x1
ch_n2_sf <- length(ch_x2_sf)
ch_z_sf <- matrix(ch_value_sf, nrow = ch_n2_sf)
ch_l_x1_sf <- seq(-1, 1, length.out = 21)
ch_line_sf <- tibble::tibble(x1 = ch_l_x1_sf)
ch_line_sf$x2 <- -2 * ch_line_sf$x1
ch_lu_sf <- 2 * ch_line_sf$x1 + ch_line_sf$x2
ch_line_sf$z <- exp(ch_lu_sf) - ch_line_sf$x1
ch_dash_sf <- list(color = "#D55E00", dash = "dash", width = 5)
ch_stops_sf <- c(0, 1)
ch_cols_sf <- c("#CCE0F0", "#0072B2")
ch_scale_sf <- list(ch_stops_sf, ch_cols_sf)
ch_eye_sf <- list(x = 1.6, y = -1.6, z = 0.9)
ch_camera_sf <- list(eye = ch_eye_sf)
ch_xaxis_sf <- list(title = "x1")
ch_yaxis_sf <- list(title = "x2")
ch_zaxis_sf <- list(title = "f(x)")
ch_scene_sf <- list(
  xaxis = ch_xaxis_sf,
  yaxis = ch_yaxis_sf,
  zaxis = ch_zaxis_sf,
  camera = ch_camera_sf
)
ch_legend_sf <- list(orientation = "h")
plotly::plot_ly() |>
  plotly::add_surface(
    x = ch_x1_sf,
    y = ch_x2_sf,
    z = ch_z_sf,
    colorscale = ch_scale_sf,
    showscale = FALSE,
    opacity = 0.8
  ) |>
  plotly::add_trace(
    data = ch_line_sf,
    x = ~x1,
    y = ~x2,
    z = ~z,
    type = "scatter3d",
    mode = "lines",
    line = ch_dash_sf,
    name = "f is linear"
  ) |>
  plotly::layout(scene = ch_scene_sf, legend = ch_legend_sf)
```

### Python

```{python}
#| label: convex-hessian-3d-python
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   Surface plot of f(x) = exp(2 x1 + x2) - x1 for x1 from -1 to 1 and x2
#|   from -3 to 3. The surface is a trough that rises steeply toward the
#|   upper right, where 2 x1 plus x2 is large, and is nearly flat on the
#|   lower left. A dashed vermilion straight line along the direction (1, -2)
#|   through the origin lies on the surface, because f is linear there.
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| fig-width: 6
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

ch_x1_3d, ch_x2_3d = np.meshgrid(np.linspace(-1, 1, 101),
                                 np.linspace(-3, 3, 101))
ch_z_3d = np.exp(2 * ch_x1_3d + ch_x2_3d) - ch_x1_3d
ch_line_x1_3d = np.linspace(-1, 1, 21)
ch_line_x2_3d = -2 * ch_line_x1_3d
ch_line_z_3d = np.exp(2 * ch_line_x1_3d + ch_line_x2_3d) - ch_line_x1_3d
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(6, 4.5))
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection="3d")
ax.plot_surface(ch_x1_3d, ch_x2_3d, ch_z_3d, color="#0072B2", alpha=0.6)
ax.plot(ch_line_x1_3d, ch_line_x2_3d, ch_line_z_3d, "--", color="#D55E00",
        label="f is linear")
ax.set_xlabel("x1")
ax.set_ylabel("x2")
ax.set_zlabel("f(x)")
ax.legend(loc="upper right")
plt.show();
```

:::

The [graph](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mcs/functions.html#def-graph) of the third [function](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mcs/functions.html#def-function) in @exm-convex-hessian,
the surface whose [level curves](vector-calculus.qmd#def-level-set) are in @fig-convex-hessian.
Along the dashed line through the origin in the [direction](vector-calculus.qmd#def-direction) $\tp{(1, -2)}$ the surface is a straight line, so the function is [linear](algebra.qmd#def-linear-function) there.
The function is therefore [convex](algebra.qmd#def-convex-function) but not [strictly convex](#def-strictly-convex).

:::
